HMW-V16: Proof Upload Zone

How might we design the proof upload experience on the vendor Job Detail page so that vendors capturing photo evidence on tablets at warehouses and terminals can do so in one tap — without hunting for a button, and without the zone cluttering the page once proof is already uploaded?
Context: The vendor app targets 768px+ tablet screens. Vendors at cargo terminals and warehouses photograph proof of service on-site — a signed POD, a stamp on a form, or a bag count photo. vendor/DESIGN.md specifies a dashed upload zone with a 📷 camera button (capture="environment") and a drag-and-drop target. The current implementation renders only a small "+ Add" button in the section header. Three design questions need resolution: (1) How prominent should the upload affordance be? (2) Should it collapse once proof is uploaded? (3) Should the camera and file-browser be separate actions or combined?

Option A: Full Upload Zone — Always Visible

Simplest
The dashed zone is always visible whenever upload is allowed (Pending or In Progress). Camera button primary, Browse secondary. Files appear as rows above the zone. The zone is always the "call to action" regardless of how many files are already uploaded.
Pros
• Unmissable — first-time upload never requires hunting
• Camera button always reachable in one tap on tablet
• Consistent — page looks the same regardless of upload state
• Drag-and-drop target always present (useful on laptop)
Cons
• Zone takes vertical space when 3–5 files already uploaded
• Redundant — the "upload more" affordance competes with the file list for attention
• Visual noise after job nears completion — vendor is reviewing, not uploading
• At 768px, the zone + 3 file rows pushes Activity Log below the fold

Option B: Smart Collapse — Zone on Empty, Compact on Fill

Recommended
When no files are uploaded, show the full dashed zone (same as Option A). Once files are added, the zone collapses: the file list is shown, and a small "+ Add" button appears in the section header. Camera and file-browse are both available from the compact button. The zone re-expands only on click.
Pros
• Full affordance when needed (0 files = zone front-and-center)
• Density-appropriate after upload (files are the content, not the zone)
• Section header "+ Add" is always reachable without scrolling
• Mirrors how logistics apps (Flexport, Lalamove) handle proof capture
• Activity Log stays above fold after upload
Cons
• Two different states require slight mental model shift
• "+ Add" button in header is smaller target than the full zone (acceptable tradeoff)
• Camera is inside the mini-menu rather than a single tap (adds one interaction)

Option C: Camera-First Action Strip

Mobile-Inspired
Replace the upload zone with a compact horizontal action strip pinned to the bottom of the Proof section. Camera (primary) and Files (secondary) sit side-by-side as small buttons. The file list renders above. No drag-and-drop target — just two tappable actions. Inspired by WhatsApp/WeChat message attachment patterns.
Pros
• Densest layout — no zone takes space, ever
• Camera and file-browse always visible in one strip
• No state change needed — same layout in empty and filled states
• Very tab-friendly on touchscreen — two large target buttons
Cons
• No empty-state affordance — first upload not obviously invited
• No drag-and-drop capability (relevant for laptop users)
• Strip can feel visually detached from the file list above
• Breaks the "smart spreadsheet" principle — feels more mobile-app than ops tool
• Unclear to first-time users: what does "Take Photo" do to the job status?

✓ Verdict: Option B — Smart Collapse

Option B wins on the core tension between discoverability and density. The full dashed zone appears only when no files exist — exactly when upload is the primary action and discoverability matters most. Once files are uploaded, the zone collapses to a small "+ Add files" button in the section header, keeping the dense smart-spreadsheet layout intact.

Implementation details for the chosen option:
• Empty state (0 files): full dashed zone with 📷 Take Photo (primary, capture="environment") + Browse Files (secondary). No add button in section header.
• Filled state (≥1 file): zone hidden. File list rows. Small "+ Add files" button in section header expands zone inline on click.
• Verified state: no upload affordance. File list + "Locked — verified by Teleport Ops." note in muted italic below last row.
• Cancelled state: same as Verified — no upload. Files viewable.
• Input attributes: <input type="file" accept="image/*,.pdf" multiple> for Browse; <input type="file" accept="image/*" capture="environment"> for Take Photo (separate hidden inputs).
• Both inputs trigger on the same handleUpload handler. Batch log entry: "Uploaded 3 files: pod-front.jpg, …".
• OH (Outbound Hub) service: upload available — hub ops teams do use the vendor app on tablets.

Open question (needs user input):
The Status Action Bar on the In Progress state already shows an "Upload Proof" button. Should clicking this button scroll to the Proof section + expand the zone, or trigger the file input directly from the status bar without scrolling? Direct-trigger is one tap fewer but bypasses the file list (vendor can't see what's already uploaded). Scroll-to-expand keeps the context. Recommendation: scroll to expand zone, but needs confirmation.
